messages:
Anya: Heads-up — we need a short RFC on gateway route matching syntax. Console UX depends on stable precedence rules and obvious override behavior.
Mike: +1. Main questions: order of host vs path vs service vs header match, and whether we allow numeric priority overrides.
Jess: For routing, my vote: evaluate host first, then path, then headers. Host scoping narrows the domain; path specificity should decide within host.
Samir: I disagree on headers after path. Consider feature flags via headers (x-redwood-tenant). They should be able to pin traffic earlier than a broad path prefix. Example: /v1/* but header X-Tier: enterprise should route to dedicated pool.
Lydia: We should formalize "specificity" rules instead of ad-hoc order. Idea: compute specificity score from (host specificity, path specificity, header match count, method match), then pick highest score. Ties broken by creation time or explicit priority.
Mike: Specificity score sounds good but UX/observability needs to show why one route won. We need telemetry keys: matched_route_id, score_components, tie_breaker_reason.
Anya: Agree on telemetry. Also we must decide supported matcher types: `exact`, `prefix`, `regex`, `wildcard` (eg `*.example.com`).
Jess: Recommend disallowing complex regex for host — only wildcard + exact. Regex allowed on path but deprioritized because it's expensive.
Samir: Also need header match types: `exists`, `exact`, `prefix`, `regex`. And add `invert` option for negative matches.
Lydia: On overrides: console allows per-route header overrides (add/replace) and per-request header passthrough. If an override changes routing keys (eg rewrite Host), it must be applied before route selection? That causes loops. I propose overrides run after route selection; rewrite only affects upstream host/service, not matching.
Mike: +1 — overrides after match avoids changing which route was picked. But we need a special boolean `rewrite_before_match: true` for exceptional cases (advanced users) with explicit warning and requires enablement flag in config.
Jess: Quotas: when a route has `quota: daily:100k` and an override routes traffic to another service, which quota applies? My preference: quota is tied to the original route handling the request (the matching route). If upstream changes, we still account against the matched route unless `quota.apply_to_upstream: true` is set.
Anya: Good. Add explicit fields in config to avoid ambiguous semantics. Below is a sample config proposal (YAML):
```yaml
routes:
  - id: route-tenant-enterprise
    host: exact: api.redwood.com
    path: prefix: /v1/
    headers:
      - name: X-Tier
        exact: enterprise
    matchers: [host, path, headers]
    priority: 50        # fallback tie-breaker only
    quota:
      daily: 100000
    overrides:
      request_headers:
        - set: [X-Forwarded-For, $client_ip]
      upstream_host: service-dedicated

  - id: route-default
    host: wildcard: '*.redwood.com'
    path: prefix: /
    priority: 10
    quota: {}
```
Samir: Nice. One more: precedence rules docs should show deterministic examples. E.g. host exact beats wildcard even if wildcard has header matches. Specificity scoring example: host_exact(+100), path_exact(+50), header_match_each(+10). Compute total.
Lydia: UX note — avoid exposing raw priority numbers to most users. Show a "match preview" in the console: input host+path+headers and show which route wins and why. Advanced view can display numeric score.
Mike: Telemetry to emit per-request: `route_id`, `score`, `score_breakdown`, `matched_rule_type` (path/prefix/regex), `override_used` (true/false), `priority_tiebreaker` (explicit|created_at).
Anya: Also add a sampling flag for full-match traces (headers/payload) to reduce volume. 
Jess: Implementation note — evaluate fast path: first check host table (exact + wildcard buckets), then for candidate routes evaluate path matchers and header matchers to compute score. Regex matches last. Keep path prefix matching O(k) using a trie.
Samir: Edge case: conflicting exact path matches for same host. Tie-breaker: creation_time (newer wins) feels surprising. I prefer explicit `priority` field; if equal, fall back to latest update. Documented behavior required.
Lydia: We'll add a linter that warns when two routes are likely ambiguous. Console should block overlapping exact matches unless user confirms.
Mike: Sounds like action items: 1) draft RFC with scoring matrix and tie-breaker rules, 2) sample YAML/JSON schema, 3) console match preview UX, 4) telemetry + quota semantics, 5) linter rules.
Anya: I'll start the RFC draft and add unit tests for the matching algorithm. Samir/Lydia/Jess can review.
deploy-bot: Config preview build succeeded for branch `route-matcher-rfc`. Staging deploy queued. :rocket:
Anya: Thanks — will post RFC link here once initial draft is in the repo.
